title: Knowledge Check 4 - Lessons 16-20
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 16-20 - Access to Records. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: An Experience Cloud community must display a read-only list of approved public Accounts to the anonymous guest. Which configuration is appropriate?
options: A permission set on the guest user
A guest-user sharing rule sharing the approved accounts to the guest user profile
An ownership-based rule to an internal group
Setting Account OWD to Public Read/Write for everyone
questions.explanation: Guest-user sharing rules are the mechanism for the guest user to see records without a login; they share to the guest profile. Permission sets and internal-group rules do not cover the guest, and org-wide relaxation is over-broad.

questions.question: An org has hit the maximum number of sharing rules for Account. Which is the recommended remediation?
options: Keep adding rules anyway
Consolidate rules by sharing more records per rule and using groups, or move to team/Apex sharing where appropriate
Delete the OWD
Create a new rule type
questions.explanation: Consolidation (fewer, broader rules to named groups) or a different mechanism (teams, Apex Managed Sharing) is the correct response to the rule-count cap - you cannot simply keep adding rules.

questions.question: Why is a newly created criteria-based sharing rule not instantly granting access?
options: The rule is invalid
Criteria-based sharing is evaluated asynchronously and may need recalculation; grants appear after processing
Sharing rules remove access first
OWD blocks it
questions.explanation: Criteria rules are evaluated asynchronously for new/changed records and edited conditions; until recalculation/processing completes, grants are stale - the expected behavior, not an error.

questions.question: An org shares high-value accounts to a recurring set of 15 analysts across two roles, and this set is reused in three sharing rules. Which structure is best?
options: Reference the 15 users individually in each rule
Create a public group with the analysts, then target that group in the rules
Create a permission set for each rule
Use a queue
questions.explanation: A public group centralizes the recurring set so one membership change updates all referencing rules. Rules cannot target individual user lists cleanly, and queues/perm sets do not solve multi-rule targeting.

questions.question: Which statement about queues is TRUE?
options: Queue members have implicit access to records in the queue
Queues grant access to all records of an object
Queues replace the role hierarchy
Queues cannot own records
questions.explanation: Queue membership grants members implicit access to the queue's records (and lets them claim them). Queues are object-specific and do not replace other sharing.

questions.question: A public group was just created but its members see no new records. What is the most likely reason?
options: Groups take 24 hours
The group is not referenced by any sharing rule or queue yet
OWD is too open
Groups require licenses
questions.explanation: A group grants nothing by itself; it only has effect when a sharing rule, queue, or permission set references it. Membership alone does not change record access.

questions.question: Partner portal users must see the Opportunities belonging to their own Account. Which configuration is appropriate?
options: A public group with a sharing rule
A sharing set mapping the portal user's Account to Opportunity access
An Account Team
Setting Opportunity OWD to Public Read Only
questions.explanation: Sharing sets use the portal user's Account/Contact relationship to grant access to related records - exactly the B2B portal pattern. Public groups and account teams do not derive from the portal user's account, and relaxing OWD over-exposes.

questions.question: Which is the correct comparison between public groups and teams?
options: Teams are org-wide; groups are per-record
Groups are reusable targets for sharing rules across populations; teams grant per-record, owner-managed access
They are interchangeable
Teams cannot be enabled on Account
questions.explanation: Public groups are reusable, population-level targets for rules; teams are per-record, owner-configured grants. They solve different scale problems and are not interchangeable.

questions.question: An org needs every member of the East-Sales group to see all Accounts owned by the West-Sales group. What is the cleanest solution?
options: An Account Team for each account
A public group (East-Sales) and an ownership-based sharing rule sharing West-Sales-owned accounts to it
A sharing set
A queue
questions.explanation: Ownership-based sharing rule to the target group (East-Sales) is the population-level solution. Per-record teams do not scale, sharing sets are for external users, and queues are for assignment.

questions.question: Several users who are not managers must collaborate on a single high-value Account, each with a defined role. Which feature fits best?
options: A public group with a sharing rule
An Account Team on that Account
A permission set with View All
Relaxing OWD
questions.explanation: Account Teams provide per-record, owner-managed collaboration with roles and access levels for exactly this ad-hoc need. Groups/rules and OWD changes are population-wide, and View All over-grants.

questions.question: After enabling 'Use Account Teams' on Opportunity, an org notices opportunities are visible to more people than expected. What is the cause?
options: OWD changed
Every Opportunity now shares to the Account Team members automatically
Sales Teams were disabled
The hierarchy was removed
questions.explanation: 'Use Account Teams' makes each Opportunity inherit the Account's team members automatically, so broad account teams widen opportunity access - the expected, if surprising, behavior.

questions.question: Which statement about Case Teams is TRUE?
options: They are org-wide sharing rules
They grant access to a specific Case for the named members with a role and access level
They require a public group
They disable the hierarchy
questions.explanation: Case Teams are per-record grants to named members on a specific case. They are not org-wide, need no group, and do not affect the hierarchy.

questions.question: Every member of the Support group must see ALL cases across the org, regardless of owner. Which mechanism is most scalable?
options: An Account Team per case
The role hierarchy
A sharing rule (ownership or criteria) to the Support group
A queue
questions.explanation: Population-wide access is best expressed as a sharing rule to the reusable Support group. Per-case teams don't scale and the hierarchy can't grant all-case access to peers.

questions.question: Which scenario is best handled by Account Teams rather than groups or the hierarchy?
options: The owner of each high-value account decides which specific people help on that account, different people per account
All analysts must see all accounts
Managers see their team's accounts
The org chart defines access
questions.explanation: Per-record, owner-selected collaboration is precisely what teams do. Fixed populations (analysts) are groups, reporting lines are the hierarchy.

questions.question: What is the primary scalability disadvantage of using teams as the main sharing mechanism across many records?
options: Teams require licenses
Each team generates a share row per member per record, which can bloat the sharing table
Teams cannot be Read Only
Teams only work on standard objects
questions.explanation: Team grants materialize a share row per member per record, so using teams broadly across large record volumes inflates sharing and hurts performance - better to use groups+rules for population access.
